Plans have started pointing at each other. Tallow revisits pumice (bodkin's revisits:), and entries anchor to other plans' entries: three in mock-control at f02528f, seven in aide at 248a2a5. Phoropter treats each of those as an anchor into a markdown file and says "no quote, so nothing to search for," while the entry it means already has a page address. This plan makes them links.

What an agent can query without reading prose (sources, verdicts, dates, and the rest from Jeff's daily in this cart) is the next cart's question, not this one's.

Decision: revisits: is a revisits link, and the revisited plan shows revisited-by

where src/render.ts file page

quote ${frontmatterRest(plan.doc.frontmatter, ['cart', 'base'])}

Because (bodkin, Jeff): bodkin names the rels and says the old plan shows revisited-by without being edited, which a generated page gets for free. Both go in the plan's facts list, and the home page says "revisits pumice" beside tallow. A revisits: naming a plan this site doesn't have is shown as written, with a plain note.

Decision: An anchor at plans/<file>.md › <entry title> resolves to that entry

where src/resolve.ts file page

quote const [file, ...path] = where.split(' › ');

Because (measured): all ten such anchors in mock-control and aide match their target entry's title exactly, backticks included. Matching is exact, the same as an answer and its guess. If no entry in that plan or as-built has the title, the page says "no entry titled this in pumice." Anchors that name entries don't make a file page for the plan's markdown.

Decision: These anchors reuse anchored-at and anchored-by

where src/render.ts file page

quote ['anchored-at', 'phoropter', 'Where in the code does this entry point? From an anchor on an entry to the page for its symbol or file.'],

Because (Claude, agreed by Jeff): where an entry points, and who points here, is one question whatever is at the far end. The plans already call these anchors, and the target page says what it is through its microdata. The profile says anchored-at can lead to an entry as well as to a symbol or file.

Decision: An entry anchor shows the target's kind and title, linked, not views at two commits

where src/site.ts file page

quote ra.note = 'no quote, so nothing to search for';

Because (Jeff, and aide's awl): a plan is frozen when committed, and an as-built when its work lands, so both ends of the anchor are frozen. Two views would show the same text twice. It's resolved at the generated commit, and the anchor names the plan it points into.

Decision: An entry anchor with a quote also shows the entry's text, the quote highlighted

Because (Claude's fallback, agreed by Jeff): grommet anchors lanyard's entry "What changed during the work goes in <plan>.as-built.md, beside it" with the quote Its entries are `Changed:`., which says which sentence it meant. It's one view, at the generated commit, and the search stays inside the target entry, as gimlet keeps a quote inside its anchor's file. If the quote isn't in the entry, it says so.

Decision: The target entry lists what anchors it, under its heading

Because (Claude, unanswered, so its fallback): the same place and shape as "Answered in the as-built": "Anchored by", then each anchoring entry, linked, with its plan's name.

Decision: An anchor at a whole plan file links to the plan's page, and keeps its quote search

Because (Claude, unanswered, so its fallback): a quote into a plan's frontmatter is evidence like any other. Untested: the only one, bodkin's anchor at tallow, is cross-repo from aide.

Decline: A transitive link from pumice's guess straight to vellum's answer

Because (Claude, unanswered, so its fallback): quince declined this as the cart's question, and two hops now cover it. Vellum's guess anchors pumice's, and is answered in vellum's as-built. A link that skips a hop would say vellum answered pumice's guess, which only vellum's prose says.

Decline: Sources, verdicts, dates, orientation, absolute URLs, and cross-plan pages

Because (Jeff and Claude): Jeff raised them in this cart, and we agreed on most of how. They're about what an agent can query, not links between plans, and a cart that wants two plans splits. They go to the shelf at conversion.

Guess: Exact entry titles are a stable enough key for anchors between plans

Answered in the as-built: held.

Disproved if: an anchor fails to match an entry it plainly means, through a typo, a rephrase, or backticks written differently. Plans are frozen, so a title can't drift after the fact; a miss can only come from how the anchor was written.
